tut_sub: Short, practical guides for getting the most out of Text 2 Speech.
tut_g1h: Getting started: your first generated voice
tut_g1p: Start with the language selector — it decides which voices you see. Pick the language your text is written in, then try two or three voices with the Preview button; voices differ a lot in warmth and pace. Type a short paragraph first, generate it, and listen. Once the voice feels right, turn on Speed or Pitch and nudge them in small steps: +10% speed suits energetic content, a slightly lower pitch often sounds more authoritative. For anything longer than a page, generate section by section and keep the same voice and settings so the parts blend.
tut_g2h: How to use the break feature
tut_g2p: Break markers insert exact silence into generated audio. Type [break:200ms] for a short beat, [break:1s] or [break:2s] for longer pauses — dramatic reveals, list items and scene changes all land better with air around them. Pressing Ctrl+B drops a [break:500ms] marker at your cursor. Markers never appear in the audio or the subtitles; you hear only the pause. A good rule of thumb: 300–600ms between sentences that change topic, 1–2 seconds between scenes. Note that Preview mode simply skips the markers, so judge final timing on the generated file.
tut_g3h: A tour of the voice collection
tut_g3p: Text 2 Speech's catalog holds 300+ neural voices across 75 languages, and each language offers several personalities — newsreader-flat, warm and conversational, bright and youthful. Names carry their region (Aria - US, Natasha - AU), and a few voices are multilingual, handling mixed-language text gracefully. Gender filtering and name search keep the list manageable. When in doubt, generate the same paragraph with three candidate voices and pick with your ears, not the names: the right voice depends on the material, not the label.

sup_sub: Most answers live in the FAQ on the home page. Still stuck? Send us the details.
sup_quick_p:
• No sound on Preview: check the browser tab isn't muted and try another voice.
• A voice sounds wrong for your text: match the Voice Language to the text language first.
• Long text is slow: split it into chapters and generate in parts.
• A result disappeared: results live only for the current browser session — download promptly.

auth_sub: Accounts are optional — the converter works fully without one. Sign in to keep your voice favorites and history in sync (rolling out with the public launch).
auth_alert_signin: Accounts arrive with the public launch. Everything on Text 2 Speech already works signed-out.
priv_intro: Text 2 Speech is designed to need as little of your data as possible. You can use the converter without an account and without giving us your name or email.
priv_s1p: Text you submit is sent to Microsoft's online speech service, which turns it into audio. The audio and subtitle files are stored on our server under a random session identifier and deleted automatically about two hours after your last generation. They are never published or indexed.
priv_s2p: We do not use cookies, analytics or advertising trackers. Your theme, interface language and the results list of the current tab are kept only in your own browser's storage.
priv_s3p: We do not sell personal data, we do not build advertising profiles, and we do not keep your generated audio after it expires.
priv_s4p: Questions about privacy: reach us through the Support page. Messages sent there (your email address and text) are kept only as long as needed to answer you.
terms_s1p: Text 2 Speech converts text you provide into synthesized speech and lets you play and download the result, together with subtitle files. The service is provided as-is, without guarantees of uninterrupted availability.
terms_s2p: Only convert text you have the right to use. Do not use generated audio to impersonate real people, deceive listeners, or break applicable laws. You are responsible for how you publish and license what you create.
terms_s3p: Personal, educational and creative use is welcome. Commercial use of generated audio is your responsibility to clear against the rights in your source text and any applicable voice-licensing rules in your jurisdiction.
terms_s4p: Features and these terms may evolve; material changes will be noted on this page with a new date.
